title: Italy fines Meta $887m for accessing Android users’ photos and videos
text:
Italy’s data protection agency has fined Facebook parent company Meta €805m ($887m) for accessing users’ photos without their specific consent.
Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement.
Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”.
In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25bn for misleading the state’s residents for more than a decade about the use of their data – a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression.
Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has imposed on a tech company.
In 2021, Amazon received a more than €1.1bn fine for breaching competition law.
That sum was subsequently reduced to €752m on appeal.
The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing.
According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery.
The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it.
In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” – about 20 million Android users in Italy – and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”.
The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”.
It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4% of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201bn in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5bn.
